newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast spot power mixed amid more outages.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast spot power mixed amid more outages.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the northeastern U.S. ended Friday mixed from Thursday's level amid more generating units taken off line for seasonal maintenance and refueling, market sources said.
The 800 megawatt (MW) Fitzpatrick nuclear station in Scriba, N.Y., was expected to shut later today for a 45-day refueling outage.

Fitzpatrick will be the third nuclear plant in the state taken out of service. It will join the 1,137 MW Nine Mile Point 2 nuclear unit, also in Scriba, which was shut for refueling and 470 MW Ginna 1 nuclear station near the town of Ontario, which was idled for diagnostic tests on its transformer.

Despite reduced capacity, participants noted some New York utilities planned to remove some fossil-fuel units from service this weekend, and bring them into "reserve shutdown" due to modest power demand.

In western NYPP, peak, non-firm electricity for the weekend was assessed as low as $14.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) and for Monday at $19.00-$20.00, lower than Thursday's range of $20.00-$21.00 for Friday delivery

Western NYPP power for non-firm delivery during weekend's light load hours was notationally pegged near $9.00 and during Monday's off-peak hours near $14.00-$15.00, compared with Thursday's quote of $14.00-$15.00 for Friday.
In the eastern part of NYPP, peak, non-firm electricity for weekend delivery was pegged at $15.00-$16.00 , and for Monday $29.00-$30.00, compared with a $29.00-$30.00 range on Thursday.
Off-peak, non-firm electricity for weekend delivery in eastern NYPP was valued at $10-$12.00 and for Monday delivery $14.50-$15.00, compared with Thursday's $14.50-$15.00.
In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), spot electricity values climbed due to the longer-than-expected shutdown of the 510 MW Vermont Yankee nuclear plant.
"The part that's keeping prices up is a little later startup of Vermont Yankee getting back to service," said a NEPOOL trader. "The Vermont Yankee (owners) were caught short."
The restart of the Vermont Yankee was pushed back to this weekend from Thursday because Nuclear Regulatory Commission needed for more fire protection data for the plant.
A 355 MW coal-fired unit at the Merrimack generating facility in Bow, N.H., will be idled later today for four weeks for maintenance.
In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity for this weekend at the Northeast Utilities border was discussed at $33.50-$34.50 and for Monday $34.50-$35.50.
Next-day, non-firm NEPOOL power for peak hour delivery was quoted at $29.00-$31.00 on Thursday.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for weekend delivery to the NU border was quoted at $19.50-$20.50 and for Monday $20.50-$21.50.
Thursday's quote for next-day, off-peak NEPOOL electricity was valued at $19.00-$20.00.
